messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty triggered: CRITICAL pd_high_5xx_rate for service=eu-inference (/generate). 5xx spike -> 8.7% over 2m (threshold 1%). Affected customers: ~3 (SaaS-prod, payments-engine, client-x). Incident INC-20263. Bridge: https://meet.redwood/INC-20263. Paging @oncall-eu now.

pagerbot: PagerDuty: page fired -> assigned to sam (oncall). Escalation policy: eu-primary -> eu-secondary.

sam: acked. I'm on it — will triage. pulling recent logs and allocation traces.

maria: thanks. any immediate customer visible impact?

sam: early numbers: error rate jumped from ~0.3% baseline to 8.7%. failing reqs ~1.2k rps at peak, 503 from runtime gpu-exec. errors concentrated on model open-quant-v2 in eu cluster.

aiden: can you paste the failing stack?

sam: logs showing OOM-ish alloc fails:
```
ERROR runtime/gpu: failed to allocate 0x2C00000 bytes gpu_alloc -> out_of_memory at kv_cache_init()
WARN serve: request handler crashed for model=open-quant-v2 shard=eu-a-12
TRACE backtrace: gpu_kernel_quantize() -> allocate_workspace() -> gpu_alloc
```

maria: hmm. open-quant-v2 was deployed 30m ago with new quant kernel.

sam: yep. hypothesis: new kernel increases working set (KV + workspace) and combined with current batching distribution pushes a subset of shards to OOM -> 5xx. quick mitigations I'm trying: reduce batching, disable kv cache for that model, and consider rollback to v1.3.

sam: running quick config changes:
```
redwoodctl model update --id open-quant-v2 --env eu --set batching.max_tokens=32
redwoodctl model update --id open-quant-v2 --env eu --set kv_cache.enabled=false
```

sam: applied both. pushing config & restarting workers on eu-a pool. will monitor.

liz: if you need a hand with host-level restarts I can take over. I'm on infra-dedicated right now.

sam: thanks — handoff incoming, I'm juggling anther page. liz, can you take ownership in PD and the bridge?

liz: taking ownership. acking incident in PD now. updating incident assignee to liz.

pagerbot: PagerDuty: incident INC-20263 acked by liz.

aiden: also let's prepare a fast rollback in case the config tweak doesn't bring errors down in next 2 min. rollback cmd: 
```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --model open-quant-v2 --to-version v1.3 --env eu
```

sam: running rollback as backup. will only execute if errors persist.

(90s pass)

liz: quick metrics — 5xx rate dropped from 8.7% -> 1.6% after batching kv disable. failing rps down to ~220. not fully back to baseline but much better.

maria: any customers still seeing errors? payments-engine reported increased failures for ~4m window. need to notify customer-success and flag for follow-up.

liz: agreed. i'll keep PD incident open and continue monitoring. if we see >2% for 5m, escalate rollback.

aiden: queue for rollback prepared, but hold for now. also capture pprof and kv state for postmortem.

sam: filed quick artifact: s3://incidents/INC-20263/logs.tar.gz and snapshots.

liz: switching traffic routing: nudged routing policy to prefer us-west for new sessions for the model to reduce load on eu pool while we stabilize.

maria: good. customer-impact summary to include in bridge notes: payments-engine ~40% of their requests failed between 14:02-14:06 UTC (approx 4m). SaaS-prod saw partial degradation (errors ~12% for ~3m). client-x brief blips. I'll open follow-up ticket for SRE -> runbook and notify CSM.

aiden: adding runbook tasks: reproduce with smaller mem headroom, test quant kernel memory footprint, add safety limit on batching per-model.

liz: marking incident as mitigated for now — keeping PD incident open for postmortem until we confirm stable for 30m. handing active work to aiden (investigation) and maria (customer comms).

sam: thanks all — sorry for the mid-shift chaos.

pagerbot: PagerDuty: incident INC-20263 status updated -> mitigated (ack: liz).

incidentbot: Created follow-up ticket INC-20263-PM with severity-high. Assigned: aiden, maria, sam. Postmortem template prefilled. Auto-suppress further pd_high_5xx_rate alerts for 15m to avoid noise.

maria: noted. will draft customer summary and link to postmortem once written.

aiden: I'll start the kernel memory tests and share findings here.

liz: keeping monitoring open. will close PD if stable after 30m. thanks team. :heart:
